header.title: GradientBorder
header.description: Full gradient stroke around the child. By default it's a masked ring on a `::before`, so the host keeps its own background. With `pad` or on a gem-system button it uses a transparent border and two background layers with `background-clip` (`padding-box` for the fill and `border-box` for the stroke). `variant` sets the motion: `flow` spins, `static` stays still and `pulse` breathes.

playground.title: Playground
playground.description: Combine the props and see the generated code. With `static`, `trigger` changes nothing: the border stays visible and still.
playground.label: Border

base.title: Basic border
base.description: With the defaults (`variant="flow"`, `thickness={2}`, `duration={4000}`) a three-color conic gradient spins around the child. The radius goes on the root; the child can use `calc(radius - var(--gemfx-gradient-border-thickness))` to stay concentric, since the variable inherits.

variants.title: Variants
variants.description: `flow` spins the gradient one full turn per cycle, at constant speed. `static` keeps it fixed at `angle`. `pulse` keeps it fixed too and breathes the stroke strength: it drops to about 30% and back.

pad.title: Fill (pad)
pad.description: Without `pad`, the effect paints only the ring and the inside shows whatever is behind it (here, the stage background). `pad` paints a color inside the stroke and replaces the host's background: use it when you want a fill without touching the child.

card.title: On a card
card.description: A `1px` stroke with a slow spin (`duration={8000}`) to highlight a card without distracting. The card keeps its own background: the ring is drawn around it.

texts.title: Everything unlocked
texts.body: Unlimited effects, custom tokens and priority support.

triggers.title: Triggers
triggers.description: With `hover` the ring is hidden and appears spinning on pointer hover or when something inside gets keyboard focus. With `click`, each click shows or hides it. In both cases the transparent border reserves the stroke's room, so the layout doesn't jump.

thickness.title: Thickness
thickness.description: `thickness` is the stroke width: a number is pixels and any CSS length works too. It's written inline as `--gemfx-gradient-border-thickness`, which the CSS uses as the width of the transparent border that reserves the stroke's room.

angle.title: Angle
angle.description: `angle` is the starting point of the conic gradient (a number is degrees). It's most visible with `static` and `pulse`, which keep it fixed; with `flow` it's where the spin starts.

colors.title: Colors
colors.description: `from`, `via` and `to` are the three gradient stops (it goes back to `from` to close the circle). Defaults: gem-system's `primary-400`, `secondary-400` and `tertiary-400`. Tokens are better.

intensity.title: Intensity
intensity.description: `intensity` sets the stroke opacity: `sm` ≈ 65%, `md` ≈ 85% and `lg` 100%. It takes a token or a number between `0` and `1`, and tokens read `--gemfx-intensity-*` from the host. With `pulse` it's the peak of the breath.

duration.title: Duration
duration.description: `duration` is one full `flow` or `pulse` cycle, in milliseconds. `delay` postpones the start of the animation.

asChild.title: No wrapper (asChild)
asChild.description: With `asChild`, the border is applied directly to the child, without adding a `div`. On gem-system's `Button` it uses the filled mode: it takes `--gem-btn-bg` (and `--gem-btn-bg-hover` on hover), so the button keeps its color, whatever the load order of gem-system's and gemffects' CSS. On any other child it uses the ring and the child keeps its own border: the effect doesn't write `border` inline and the transparent border that reserves the stroke lives in `:where()`. The ring is drawn just outside the `padding-box`, over that border: on the card (`thickness={1}`, `trigger="hover"`) you see its gray border until you hover it.

state.title: Paused and disabled
state.description: `isPaused` freezes the spin (or the breath) in place. `isDisabled` hides the stroke (without changing the size) and keeps the content interactive.

callbacks.title: Events
callbacks.description: `onGradientBorder` fires when the border turns on (on pointer enter or keyboard focus with `hover`, on click with `click` or on mount with `always`) and `outGradientBorder` when it turns off, with the reason in `event.reason`. The button still receives clicks.

texts.body: Hover the card (or Tab to the button) to turn the border on and click the button.

header.title: GradientBorder API
header.description: Reference for the props, inheritance, accessibility, CSS classes and variables, and exported types of `GradientBorder`.

demos.title: Demos
demos.description: Playground and examples for every variant, trigger and option.

import.title: Import
import.description: Import it from `@gem-org/gemffects/gradient-border` with its `gradient-border.css`, or from the root if you already load `styles.css`.

inheritance.title: Inheritance
inheritance.body: Accepts the HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement> attributes (except color) and passes them to the root div (or to the child, with asChild). onClick, onPointerEnter, onPointerLeave, onFocus and onBlur run before the effect's internal logic. The effect doesn't write border inline. In ring mode, the transparent border as wide as the stroke lives in :where() along with the rest of the base layout (display, position, color), so any host class (or the child's own border, with asChild) overrides it. In filled mode (pad or a .gem-button) the CSS forces the transparent border, because the stroke is painted on it. With pad, background-color: transparent is also written inline after style; without pad, the host's background is left alone.

items.reducedMotion: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the flow spin and the pulse breath stop; the border stays fixed at angle, at full strength.
items.ignoreReducedMotion: ignoreReducedMotion (or the gemfx-ignore-reduced-motion class on an ancestor) keeps the animation. Only use it when essential.
items.decorative: The stroke is a ::before with pointer-events: none (or a background of the element itself, with pad or on a button): it adds no nodes, isn't announced and doesn't block clicks.
items.focus: With trigger="hover" the border also shows when the host or something inside gets keyboard focus (:focus-visible), and the events fire just like with the pointer. With click the root isn't focusable: the keyboard only turns it on when the click comes from a control inside (Enter or Space on a button).
items.contrast: A decorative border doesn't replace the focus indicator. If you use it on a button, keep its :focus-visible; gem-system buttons use box-shadow, which stays visible.

items.root: Root. `isolation: isolate` and the animation. `inline-flex`, `position: relative`, `color: inherit` and the transparent border as wide as the stroke live in `:where()` (zero specificity), so a host class overrides them.
items.variant: Active variant. `static` removes the animation and `pulse` swaps it for the breath.
items.padded: Added with `pad`. Swaps the ring for two background layers: the fill on `padding-box` and the stroke on `border-box`, and forces the transparent border as wide as the stroke. On a `.gem-button` the same mode is used without this class.
items.trigger: Active trigger, only with `flow` and `pulse`. Sets `cursor: pointer`.
items.on: Added while the border is on with `click`.
items.paused: Added with `isPaused`. Pauses the animation with `animation-play-state`.
items.inactive: Added with `isActive={false}` or `isDisabled`. Hides the ring (`opacity: 0`) and removes the animation; in filled mode it paints the stroke with the `pad` color.
items.surface: Wraps the child (`z-index: 1`). With `asChild`, the class goes on the child itself.

cssVariables.title: CSS variables
cssVariables.description: Thickness, angle and timing are written inline on every render. `from`, `via`, `to`, `pad` and `intensity` are only written when you pass the prop, and `--gemfx-gradient-border-stroke` never is: you can override those from a class.

items.colors: The three gradient stops. Set by `from`, `via` and `to`.
items.pad: `padding-box` fill in filled mode. Set by `pad`; on a `.gem-button`, `--gem-btn-bg` (and `--gem-btn-bg-hover` on `:hover`). Unused in ring mode.
items.stroke: The whole stroke gradient (a `conic-gradient`), in the ring and in filled mode. Override it from a class to use more colors; keep `--gemfx-gradient-border-angle` and `--gemfx-gradient-border-turn` so it keeps spinning, and `--gemfx-gradient-border-strength` if you want `intensity` and `pulse` to apply.
items.thickness: Stroke width and width of the transparent border that reserves it. Set by `thickness`; default `2px`.
items.angle: Starting gradient angle. Set by `angle`; default `120deg`.
items.turn: Animated rotation (registered with `@property` as `<angle>`). The `flow` animation moves it.
items.intensity: Base stroke intensity. Set by `intensity`; default `var(--gemfx-intensity-md, 55%)`.
items.strength: Opacity of each stop (via `color-mix`): `min(100%, intensity + 30%)` times `--gemfx-gradient-border-breath`.
items.breath: `pulse` breath (registered with `@property` as `<number>`): goes from `1` to `0.3` and back. It's `1` in the other variants.

tokens.title: Tokens
tokens.description: Global variables GradientBorder reads as defaults. You can redefine them on the root with a class.

items.palette: Default `from`, `via` and `to` colors (with neon, magenta and amber fallbacks).
items.btnBg: Default and `:hover` fill on a gem-system `Button`. Each variant sets them.
items.intensity: Values for `sm`, `md` and `lg` (`35%`, `55%` and `80%`). The default uses `md` and the prop writes `var(--gemfx-intensity-*)` for tokens, so redefining them changes the stroke strength.

content.title: Content
content.description: Which content gets the border and where the effect is mounted.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.description: Motion, colors, fill, thickness, angle and intensity.

timing.title: Timing
timing.description: Animation cycle and delay, in milliseconds.

state.title: Trigger and state
state.description: When it shows and animates, how it pauses and how it turns off.

events.title: Events
events.description: `event.reason` can be `always`, `hover`, `click`, `inactive`, `disabled` or `unmount`. With `static` they behave as with `always`: `onGradientBorder` fires on mount.

items.children: Content inside the border. It keeps its background: the ring is drawn around it.
items.asChild: Applies the border to the single child, without a wrapping `div`. Designed for gem-system's `Button`; in ring mode, the child keeps its own border.
items.variant: `flow` spins, `static` stays fixed at `angle` and `pulse` breathes the stroke strength with a fixed angle.
items.from: First gradient stop. A token is better; default `primary-400`.
items.pad: Fill inside the stroke. When set, it replaces the host's background. Without `pad` only the ring is painted and the host keeps its background; on a gem-system button `--gem-btn-bg` is used.
items.thickness: Stroke width. A number is pixels.
items.angle: Starting gradient angle. A number is degrees.
items.intensity: Stroke opacity (`sm` ≈ 65%, `md` ≈ 85%, `lg` 100%). Token or number between `0` and `1`. With `pulse`, it's the peak.
items.duration: One full `flow` or `pulse` cycle. Negative values are treated as `0`.
items.trigger: `always` always animates, `hover` shows the border on pointer hover or keyboard focus inside and `click` shows and hides it with each click. `static` ignores it.
items.isActive: Shows the border. When `false` it hides it (without changing the size) and `outGradientBorder` receives `inactive`.
items.isPaused: Freezes the `flow` spin or the `pulse` breath.
items.isDisabled: Hides the border; the child stays interactive. `outGradientBorder` receives `disabled`.
items.ignoreReducedMotion: Keeps the animation even when the user prefers reduced motion. Only when essential.
items.onGradientBorder: Fires when the border turns on: on mount with `always` (or `static`), on pointer enter or keyboard focus with `hover` or on click with `click`.
items.outGradientBorder: Fires when it turns off: on pointer or focus leave, on a second click, when deactivated or on unmount.
items.style: Inline styles for the root. The effect's variables (and the background, if you pass `pad`) are written after it. A `border` here is kept; in filled mode better leave it alone, because the stroke is painted on that border.
items.ref: Ref to the root (the `div`, or the child with `asChild`).
